claims.title: Message packing, fields and signing match stored executed-reference vectors
claims.boundary: Named vector corpus; not live delivery.

claims.title: Direct and opportunistic delivery exchange messages with Python
claims.boundary: Pinned peer and the sizes/methods selected by each case.

claims.title: Propagation retrieval and peer synchronization exchange stored messages
claims.boundary: Peer authorization and non-default transfer limits remain test-specific.

claims.title: Impaired mixed transport paths retain delivery and cancellation behavior
claims.boundary: Named Python/.NET transport topologies, not RF.

claims.title: Ticket and ratchet persistence works across reference handoffs
claims.boundary: Selected reply-ticket and ratchet rotation/restart scenarios.

claims.title: Local router lifecycle, cancellation and rejection continue service
claims.boundary: Managed integration tests; not Python interoperability.

claims.title: Daemon rejects invalid arguments and configuration before opening a node
claims.boundary: Managed argument boundary plus optional published configuration rejection; neither alone proves daemon interoperability.

claims.title: Published daemon receives Python delivery and preserves its inbox over restart
claims.boundary: One-way daemon receipt; not bidirectional propagation.

claims.title: Published propagation daemon supports retrieval, control and autonomous peer recovery
claims.boundary: Six-case suite's explicit policy, timing and peer settings; no exhaustive failure matrix.

claims.title: Frames and signalling match the executed-reference corpus
claims.boundary: Stored vectors and malformed input; not live audio.

claims.title: Installed native codecs match reference bitstreams
claims.boundary: Installed Opus/Codec2 versions and profile corpus; not audio hardware.

claims.title: Stream packets, codecs and signals exchange over mixed paths
claims.boundary: Named direct/Python/.NET transport topologies only.

claims.title: Python telephone setup, profiles, teardown and rejection recover
claims.boundary: Virtual audio; no physical quality claim.

claims.title: Managed audio processing and device ownership preserve local contracts
claims.boundary: Fakes and executed vectors, not physical devices.

claims.title: Published phone validates CLI and persists configuration/identity
claims.boundary: Platform-specific CLI/process cases.

claims.title: Two published native phones exchange codec frames and recover
claims.boundary: Windows synthetic silence or Linux virtual audio; no Python peer claim.

claims.title: Published phone originates and answers actual Python calls
claims.boundary: Linux virtual audio, not physical hardware.

claims.title: Native telemetry format rejects unknown versions and publishes directly and through a transport hop
claims.boundary: A .NET-only format, no upstream compatibility target.

claims.title: Native address, Micron subset and state-store contracts remain bounded
claims.boundary: Initial textual subset; not full Micron/Urwid parity.

claims.title: Published terminal client retains identity and local state
claims.boundary: Native CLI/process behavior, no reference peer.

claims.title: Actual upstream node serves pages/files and exchanges messages with native client
claims.boundary: Linux single-hop TCP; declared upstream dependency minimums exceed tested pins.

claims.title: Original desktop navigation, preferences, validation and shutdown preserve application state
claims.boundary: Original Avalonia UI subset, not pixel or feature parity.

claims.title: Application core exchanges direct text messages with pinned Python LXMF
claims.boundary: LXMF peer, not the complete upstream Sideband GUI or shared-instance coexistence.

claims.title: Published native application preserves identity and renders validation feedback
claims.boundary: Actual window/renderer on selected display; no hardware audio.

claims.title: Actual reference imports reject source drift and incorrect checkouts
claims.boundary: Module/revision/hash verification, not publisher authentication or a fresh network fetch.

claims.title: Voice, attachments, maps, telemetry, plugins and LAN repository mirror
claims.boundary: Not implemented; no tests imply support.

claims.title: Physical RF mesh and physical audio interoperability
claims.boundary: One read-only identified board and synthetic audio do not establish this.

tests.pattern: *receives and persists a Python LXMF message*
Native rnphone configuration and phonebook persistence.*
Two Windows native rnphone processes without audio hardware.*
Two native rnphone processes with isolated virtual audio.*
Native rnphone against actual Python Telephone.*
